answer: Each agent must lock a refundable work bond before it can offer services at the wharf marketplace, and every finished job adds a signed entry to a public atlas of reputation. A newcomer with no history can only take small jobs, and a lantern audit — a random spot-check by established peers — slashes the bond if the work is fake. Spinning up a thousand fake identities therefore costs a thousand bonds plus the real work needed to build each reputation, while one honest agent pays once and earns steadily.
